frontmatter.title: Overview

blocks.content: Aspose.Note is a Python library for reading, manipulating, and exporting Microsoft OneNote (.one) files without requiring Microsoft Office. It enables developers to build note-taking workflows directly into Python applications—supporting tasks like batch processing, content extraction, and PDF export.

Key capabilities include loading `.one` files, iterating over pages, searching by title, and exporting to PDF. The API exposes core properties like `display_name` and `source_path`, and methods such as `get_page()`, `find_pages()`, and `export_pdf()`. PDF export requires the optional `reportlab` dependency.

from aspose_note_foss import Document, SaveFormat

doc = Document("MyNotes.one")

for page in doc:
    title = page.Title.TitleText.Text if page.Title and page.Title.TitleText else "(untitled)"
    print(title)

doc.Save("out.pdf", SaveFormat.Pdf)

from onenote import Document

doc = Document.open("notes.one")

print(doc.display_name)
print(doc.page_count)

for page in doc:

blocks.content: Aspose.Note for Python is a 100% free and open-source library that enables developers to read, search, and export OneNote `.one` files directly from Python note-taking applications or professional workflows. It integrates seamlessly into existing Python environments and supports common operations like loading sections, iterating over pages, and exporting to PDF.

items: Open and iterate over `.one` section files using `Document.open()` and `for page in doc` syntax
Search pages by title using `find_pages()` with optional case sensitivity
Export entire sections to PDF with `export_pdf()` — ideal for generating reports or sharing notes
Access core metadata such as `page_count`, `display_name`, and `source_path` on loaded documents

blocks.content: Install Aspose.Note for Python to read Microsoft OneNote (.one) files using the official public API. Only the `aspose.note` package is supported, and it exposes a clean, Aspose.Note-shaped interface for programmatic access to OneNote content.

from onenote import Document

doc = Document.open("MyNotes.one")
print(f"Pages: {doc.page_count}")
for page in doc:
    print(f"- {page.title}")

Get started quickly with Aspose.Note for Python by installing the package and exploring its familiar API surface, inspired by Aspose.Note for .NET. The library supports core operations like opening `.one` files, iterating pages, outlines, and images, and exporting to PDF using optional dependencies.
